items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates the mechanical performance, freeze–thaw durability, and microstructural characteristics of marl soil treated with iron and steel cooling water sludge (CWS) and polypropylene fibers (PPFs). The CWS used in this study is an Fe-rich industrial by-product generated from the cooling water circulation system of an iron and steel production facility. In an initial screening stage, mixtures containing 5–30% CWS and 0.2–1.4% PPF were evaluated using 7-day unconfined compressive strength (UCS) tests. The highest UCS values within the investigated ranges were obtained at 15% CWS and 1% PPF, increasing the UCS of untreated marl from approximately 254 kPa to 430 kPa with 15% CWS and 450 kPa with 1% PPF. These dosages were subsequently selected for the freeze–thaw durability program. Untreated and treated specimens were conditioned or cured for 7, 28, and 90 days and subjected to up to 10 freeze–thaw cycles. Repeated freeze–thaw exposure reduced the UCS of all the specimens; however, the magnitude of deterioration depended strongly on the treatment type and the curing duration. Untreated marl exhibited strength losses of 27.7–31.5% after 10 cycles. The 15% CWS-treated specimens showed comparatively stable freeze–thaw resistance, with strength losses of 20.5–22.6%, whereas the performance of 1% PPF was strongly curing-time dependent, with the strength loss decreasing from 58.2% at 7 days to 27.5% at 90 days. The combined 15% CWS + 1% PPF treatment exhibited the most favorable response at 90 days, with a strength loss of 20.7% after 10 freeze–thaw cycles. The SEM observations qualitatively indicated a comparatively more compact and continuous matrix in the treated specimens, while the XRD patterns showed mineralogical differences associated with CWS incorporation; however, specific cementitious or hydration products could not be conclusively confirmed. Overall, the combined CWS–PPF treatment improved the mechanical integrity and freeze–thaw durability of marl soil and may provide a practical route for the beneficial reuse of an iron and steel industry by-product, provided that its environmental suitability is confirmed.</jats:p>
title: Freeze–Thaw Performance of Marl Soil Stabilized with Iron and Steel Cooling Water Sludge and Polypropylene Fibers: Toward Sustainable By-Product Reuse

items.abstract: <jats:p>The resilience and stability of industrial supply chains are the core pillars of the sustainable development of the global economy, and also an important foundation for achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals of “Responsible Consumption and Production” and “Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure”. To address the problem that traditional industrial supply chain risk assessment systems have fixed indicators and static weights, which are difficult to adapt to complex scenarios such as dynamic adjustments of supply chain nodes, fluctuations in market demand and changes in geopolitical patterns, and thus restrict the construction of sustainable supply chain resilience, this paper proposes a comprehensive indicator-weight dynamic evolution algorithm for industrial supply chain risk assessment systems. Firstly, the evolutionary characteristics and trigger rules of the industrial supply chain risk system are defined. Indicator-weight evolution is performed when the original indicator system can no longer meet the evaluation requirements. The Delphi method combined with the actual risk characteristics of the supply chain is adopted to determine the candidate indicator set. The candidate indicators are screened using the grey relational analysis algorithm and the entropy weight-variation coefficient method to construct the evolved risk indicator set. Secondly, an improved DEMATEL model is used to analyze the causal relationships among the evolved indicators. Evolutionary analysis of the original indicator weights is carried out according to the influence degrees between indicators, so as to obtain the evolved indicator weights and realize the dynamic linkage update of evaluation weights. This study conducts a case analysis using publicly available aggregated synthetic data on supply chain disruptions and resilience and compares the proposed method with the entropy weight–analytic hierarchy process (EW-AHP) and dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) methods. The performance of the methods is evaluated in terms of the consistency of indicator weights or relative importance, computational time, out-of-sample prediction performance, and retrospective analysis of a representative disruption event scenario. The results indicate that, under the current case and parameter settings, the proposed method can reconstruct the risk indicator system and coordinate indicator and weight updates, demonstrating certain advantages in computational efficiency and risk factor identification in the specified comparative experiments. It should be noted, however, that the current validation relies primarily on publicly available synthetic aggregated data and retrospective event-scenario analysis. Therefore, the evidence is insufficient to directly establish the risk-warning benefits or improvements in operational response efficiency that the method might deliver in real-world enterprise settings. This study provides a methodological framework for the coordinated updating of indicators and weights in dynamic industrial supply chain risk assessment. Its applicability across industries and practical effectiveness require further validation using independent data sources and actual enterprise operational data.</jats:p>
title: An Integrated Indicator-Weight Evolution Method for Sustainable Industrial Supply Chains in Dynamic Scenarios

items.abstract: <jats:p>Studies have shown that the use of readily available and easily prepared modifiers can control the specific properties of the starch material, targeting those that are most beneficial for specific applications. Starch is one of the materials poised to replace traditional polymers in food packaging and wound dressings. However, its functional properties, including barrier properties, antibacterial and mechanical properties, need to be improved. Films made of kuzu starch cross-linked with citric acid and plasticised with glycerol were modified with various modifiers: Kalanchoe pinnata extract, silver nanoparticles in this extract, an extract additionally stabilised with a biopreservative, and chitosan. The effect of these modifiers on the chemical structure and morphology of the starch films, as well as on their barrier properties, thermal, mechanical, and bacteriostatic properties, was determined. Only films containing silver nanoparticles produced clear inhibition zones against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. Chitosan-containing films exhibited weak antibacterial activity, while no measurable inhibition zones were observed for unmodified starch films or films containing only Kalanchoe pinnata extract. No viable yeasts or moulds were detected on the film surfaces during the 14-day storage period under the conditions of the study. The starch film with chitosan had the highest tensile strength, while film with the Kalanchoe pinnata extract had the highest elongation. The film made of starch with Kalanchoe pinnata extract had the highest water vapour transmission rate and the lowest contact angle, while the film made of starch with chitosan had the highest barrier properties.</jats:p>
title: Green Modifiers for Sustainable Kuzu Starch-Based Films: Tailoring Functional Properties

items.abstract: <jats:p>With the development of dual-channel supply chains, consumers have more purchasing options, and reference price effects have become increasingly important in shaping their purchasing decisions. To attract consumers, some suppliers and retailers need to adjust their pricing strategies and provide measures such as return services to gain more profits. To address these problems, considering that the reference price effect and return service level are important factors affecting the supply chain, we construct game-theoretic models for a manufacturer-dominated dual-channel supply chain comprising one manufacturer and one retailer, use them to examine the optimal decisions, and analyze the effects of the reference price effect and return service level on the supply chain. Then, a two-part pricing contract is developed. The results show that, within the feasible parameter region, a higher return service level improves the total supply chain profit. In the parameter regions examined, a stronger reference price effect increases the manufacturer’s online channel demand and revenue, whereas the retailer’s offline channel demand and revenue tend to decrease when the return service level is relatively low. Furthermore, the manufacturer’s profit increases, while the retailer’s profit may decline at relatively low return service levels. A sufficiently high return service level can mitigate this adverse effect. The proposed two-part pricing contract yields a feasible interval of fixed transfer fees within which the profit conflict between the manufacturer and the retailer can be resolved.</jats:p>
title: Pricing and Coordination of a Dual-Channel Supply Chain Considering Price Reference Effect and Return Service

items.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a transformative technology for enhancing Environmental Management Systems (EMSs); however, successful implementation remains constrained by organizational, technological, and governance-related challenges. While the existing literature has largely examined AI adoption, environmental management, and supply chain sustainability separately, limited attention has been given to how organizational readiness, practitioner involvement, data integrity, and responsible AI governance collectively influence AI-enabled Environmental Management System (EMS) implementation and continuous improvement. This study addresses this gap through a qualitative case study involving three focus group discussions with eighteen (18) cross-functional professionals such as quality managers, SHERQ officers, supply chain analysts, sustainability managers, HSE managers, and continuous improvement specialists. Upon conducting the third focus group discussion, sampling ceased, thereby reaching thematic saturation, and data was analyzed using thematic analysis. Using reflective thematic analysis, and the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework as a theoretical lens, the study identifies two themes: challenges related to AI implementation, operational efficiency and data integrity. The findings reveal that organizational readiness, practitioner involvement, data quality, system integration, and governance mechanisms are critical enablers of successful AI implementation, while fragmented systems, manual reporting, privacy concerns, AI reliability, and resistance to change remain significant barriers. Building on these findings, the study proposes an extended AI-driven EMS Continuous Improvement Framework that integrates TOE dimensions with responsible AI governance, emphasizing human oversight, transparency, accountability, and ethical AI use. The study presents a practical implementation pathway to guide organizations from readiness assessment and data standardization to AI governance and continuous improvement. By extending the TOE framework to the context of AI-enabled EMS, the study contributes to theoretical and practical knowledge by demonstrating that sustainable AI adoption depends not only on technological capability, but also on practitioner involvement, data integrity, and governance structures that support continuous improvement.</jats:p>
title: AI-Driven Environmental Management System: Assessing Implementation, Practitioner Involvement, and Opportunities for Continuous Improvement

items.abstract: <jats:p>Urban areas are shaped by physical, social, cultural, and economic dynamics, requiring sustainable planning approaches that balance liveability, accessibility, and cultural continuity. This study examines Atakum, a rapidly urbanised district in Samsun, Turkey, which has evolved from a coastal resort into one of the densest urban areas in the Black Sea region. Focusing on the Türkiş region, Atakum’s earliest intensively developed residential area, this study evaluates urban morphological sustainability through typo-morphological analysis within the framework of New Urbanism. The methodology integrates a literature review, spatial analysis, morphological mapping, and space syntax to assess building typologies, block structures, green space distribution, pedestrian accessibility, and transportation networks. The findings revealed imbalances in public and green space provision, inadequate pedestrian infrastructure, and challenges related to density, sunlight access, and street hierarchy. Despite mixed land uses and commercial vitality, deficiencies in walkability and environmental quality contribute to fragmented urban patterns, undermining sustainability and quality of life.</jats:p>
title: Toward a Sustainable Urban Morphology: A Critical Examination of Atakum City Centre
